question.text: The eccentric angle in the first quadrant of a point on the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{10}+\frac{y^{2}}{8}=1$ at a distance 3 units from the centre of the ellipse is

solution.text:
Let $P(\sqrt{10} \cos \theta, \sqrt{8} \sin \theta)$ be the required point
on $\frac{x^{2}}{10}+\frac{y^{2}}{8}=1$
Whose distance from centre (0,0) is 3 units. $\therefore 10 \cos ^{2} \theta+8 \sin ^{2} \theta=9=9\left(\sin ^{2} \theta+\cos ^{2} \theta\right)$
$$
\Rightarrow \quad \tan ^{2} \theta=1 \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{4}
$$
